proof: The one-inclusion density lemma applies to every subfamily: each induced subgraph has density at most $\mathrm{VC}(\mathcal H)$. The densest-subgraph-twice parameter is twice this maximum density, so it is at most $2\,\mathrm{VC}(\mathcal H)$.
name: VC Dimension / Densest Subgraph (twice)
witness_verification: For #classes/addressing with n>=4, the established endpoint values or bounds, in parameter order, are $\lfloor\log_2 n\rfloor$ and $0$. The first parameter divided by one plus the second tends to infinity. Thus no reverse affine-linear bound holds. See the database-owned endpoint value proofs.
